To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a cell-free, protein-synthesis system has been prepared from Rhodosp. rubrum cells, that this system is active and that it is not very different between the photosynthesizing and the nonphotosynthesizing cells.
the protein-synthesising activity of R. rubrum grown under different conditions is similar.

an active in vitro protein synthesizing system has been established from Rhodosp. rubrum grown under photosynthetic or under heterotrophic conditions, and that the differences in protein synthesizing activity between the two systems have been studied in regard to the requirements of various chemicals, and the response to inhibitors of protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the cell-free, protein-sythesizing system of Rhodospirilium rubrum.
the study of the mechanism of protein synthesis in the photosynthetic bacterium, Rhodospirllum rubrum, and the effect of light and oxygen on this process.
the development of an active in vitro protein synthesizing system of R. rubrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photosynthetic system is more active than the heterotrophic one.
the photosynthetic R. rubrum system is not significantly different from the heterotrophic R. rubrum protein-synthesizer.
no major differences in protein-synthesis exist between photosynthetic and nonphotosynthetic R. rubrum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R. rubrum grown photosynthetically and heterotrophically have essentially identical protein-synthesizers.

the cell-free, protein-synthetizing system of Rhodospirillun rubrum is very similar to those of E. coli and R. sphaeroides, and that the differences between the photosynthesizing and the heterotrophie systems are not very significant.
the protein-synthesising systems of photosynthetic or the heterotrophic R. rubrum are similar in many respects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell-free, protein-synthesis systems of R. rubrum are very similar, if not identical, to the cell-free systems developed from Escherichia coli and other bacterial species.
a cell-free, protein-synthesis system can be developed from Rhodspirillum rubrum that is active and can be used for the study of protein synthesis.

a protein-synthesising system can be obtained from R. rubrum cells that are grown under either photosynthesis or heterotrophic growth conditions, with only minor differences in the protein-synthesing activity.
